title: Theo Thinks 7% Doubles Money in 72 Years 😂
description:
Theo found the Rule of 72 and decided his $10,000 at 7% would double in 72 years. Nora's fix: 72 is the number you DIVIDE by your rate. 72 ÷ 7 ≈ 10, so it doubles roughly every 10 years: $20K, $40K, $80K... and after 72 years it has doubled about seven times, to about $1.3 million ($1,305,065). At 6% it's 72 ÷ 6 = 12 years.

Takeaway: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ your yearly rate.

What rate are you earning, and how many years does that give you? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration only: example 7% a year (not a forecast), compounded yearly, no fees, taxes, withdrawals or new deposits. The Rule of 72 is an estimate (exact doubling time at 7% is 10.24 years). Real returns vary and can be negative. This is not financial advice.
